zones.name: Neck & Cervical Spine
zones.description: Forward head posture creates excessive strain on the cervical spine and surrounding musculature. For every inch the head moves forward, the load on the neck muscles effectively doubles, leading to chronic tension, headaches, and nerve compression.
dos: Maintain neutral spine alignment while sitting
Perform chin tucks to strengthen deep cervical flexors
Use a supportive pillow that maintains the natural curve of the neck
donts: Avoid looking down at phones for extended periods (Text Neck)
Don't sleep on your stomach with your head turned sharply
Avoid propping your head up with too many pillows while reading/watching TV in bed

zones.name: Shoulder Girdle
zones.description: Rounded shoulders and protracted scapulae are common issues stemming from prolonged desk work. This alters the mechanics of the shoulder joint, increasing the risk of impingement and rotator cuff strain.
dos: Strengthen rhomboids and middle traps (scapular retraction)
Sleep on your back or on the unaffected side with a supportive pillow between arms
donts: Avoid sleeping directly on the affected shoulder
Avoid lifting heavy objects away from the body's center of gravity

zones.name: Thoracic Spine (Upper Back)
zones.description: Thoracic kyphosis (excessive rounding of the upper back) is often linked to poor postural habits. It restricts mobility, impacts breathing capacity, and contributes to neck and lower back pain as the body compensates.
dos: Use a foam roller for thoracic extensions
Incorporate regular movement breaks during desk work
Ensure your chair provides adequate mid-back support
donts: Avoid sitting without back support for long durations
Don't perform heavy overhead lifts without proper thoracic mobility
Avoid sleeping on overly soft, sagging mattresses that exacerbate rounding

zones.name: Lumbar Spine (Lower Back)
zones.description: The lumbar spine bears the majority of the body's weight. Poor seated posture or inadequate spinal support during sleep can flatten or exaggerate the natural lumbar curve, increasing disc pressure and straining ligaments.
dos: Maintain a neutral pelvic tilt while sitting or standing
Engage core muscles to stabilize the spine
Sleep on a mattress that conforms to your body's natural curves while providing firm support
donts: Avoid prolonged sitting, especially in slouched positions
Don't lift with a rounded back (lift with your legs)
Avoid sleeping on your stomach without a pillow under your pelvis to prevent hyperextension
